title: Americans Put Food First on Vacation
paragraphs: When Americans go on vacation, the top thing they think about isn't beaches or famous places. It's where to eat!

A new survey by the National Restaurant Association asked more than 1,000 US adults about their travel plans. Among those planning an overnight trip in America, 98% say they'll visit a restaurant during their vacation.

OK, maybe it's not so surprising that almost everyone plans to eat at a restaurant when they're not at home. But that's still more than the 85% who plan to go shopping, the 83% planning to go sightseeing, and the 76% planning to spend time at the beach.

And going to a restaurant doesn't just mean sitting down inside to eat. Ninety-three percent plan to do that, but almost as many — 90% — also plan to use drive-thrus, order takeout or have food delivered. Another 84% plan to stop at coffee shops or snack stores.
Many Americans also want to try local food. Nearly eight out of 10 travelers say they'll eat or drink things that are famous in the places they visit, such as New York pizza or Los Angeles tacos.
But price is also important. Seven out of 10 travelers say they'll look for restaurants with discounts or other special deals.
When choosing where to eat, 87% go to places recommended by family and friends. Many also look to hotel staff, online reviews or social media to help them choose.
For many Americans, a vacation isn't only about where they go — it's also about what they eat and the new foods they try along the way!
